Diclorix

A diclofenac-based veterinary anti-inflammatory injectable.

Diclorix extends the supportive-care range with a diclofenac-based solution for injection. The supplied information states 5.39 g diclofenac sodium per 100 ml, equivalent to 5 g diclofenac base, in a 100 ml vial.

A closer look at Diclorix.

The product presentation focuses on veterinary inflammation and pain-care contexts. The underlying cause of pain, the animal’s species and the authorised conditions of use must guide any treatment discussion. A pain-care product does not replace investigation of the clinical problem.

What is in the formulation?

ComponentAvailable formulation detail
Diclofenac sodium5.39 g per 100 ml
Diclofenac base equivalent5 g per 100 ml

The product’s care focus.

  • Diclofenac sodium is the named ingredient.
  • The stated quantity is 5.39 g per 100 ml, equivalent to 5 g diclofenac base.
  • A gold-labelled 100 ml veterinary injectable presentation.

Presentation, route and administration.

Veterinary injectable presentation; use only the authorised route specified for the exact product.

Product-specific directions

A complete numerical dose is not clearly established by the supplied material. The veterinarian must confirm the authorised amount, route and duration.

Build a more useful care conversation.

Prepare these details when discussing Diclorix with your veterinary team.

  • Describe the source, duration and severity of the animal’s signs.
  • Provide details of other medicines and relevant health history.
  • Confirm species restrictions, the precise administration plan and any withdrawal requirements.

Before you take the next step.

What should I request for Diclorix?+

Ask for the current product specification, the available pack size and directions for your species and market. For a commercial enquiry, include your organisation, country and the quantity or documentation you need.

Does a care category establish suitability for my animal?+

No. The exact formulation, animal’s condition and local product authorisation matter. The treating veterinarian should confirm suitability, administration and any applicable food-production withdrawal requirements.

For veterinary professionals. Product information is an overview; the current locally authorised instructions and prescribing veterinarian determine use. Pack presentation may vary.
